headline: Nifty slipped 0.54% but *1,969 stocks fell*
subline: FIIs sold, DIIs bought, and the broader market took the heavier hit.
hero_text: FIIs sold Rs 3,458.7 Cr in cash while DIIs bought Rs 2,891.32 Cr. Domestic money absorbed most of the foreign exit.

why.title: Decliners swamped advancers
why.desc: Nearly three stocks fell for every one that rose.

why.title: FMCG sold off hard
why.desc: Nifty FMCG fell 1.41%, with Nestle the heaviest Nifty 50 loser.

why.title: IT gave back some gains
why.desc: Nifty IT fell 1.05% after a strong five day run.

why.title: No single trigger emerged
why.desc: Selling came without a named catalyst. Smallcaps fell hardest.

sector_reasons.PSU Bank: Held a small bid while the tape fell
sector_reasons.Healthcare: Cipla kept it flat against the slide
sector_reasons.FMCG: Nestle fell 2.78% to lead the drag
sector_reasons.Energy: Reliance fell 2.03% and pulled it lower

bonus_text: 1,969 stocks fell and 700 rose. Only 14 of the 50 Nifty names advanced, so the index dip understated the damage.
movers_note_gainers: Bajaj Finance led, with Cipla and ICICI Bank close behind.
movers_note_losers: Nestle fell most. Eternal and HDFC Life followed.
watch_text: Friday: TechM trades ex dividend. The Nifty close sits below the max pain level of 22,850.
lessons: A small index dip hid a heavy tape. Nearly three stocks fell for every one that rose.
Five days split the market. IT gained 6.33% while smallcaps lost 5.47%.
FIIs held a net short of 280,300 index futures contracts, matching their cash selling.
Defensives gave no cover. FMCG slid while pharma and PSU banks barely moved.
alert_text: Euro flash PMIs land at 16:45 IST on Friday. US flash PMIs follow at 23:15 IST.
cta_headline: A thin dip, a heavy tape. *Save it for Friday*.
cta_sub: Full wrap every evening. Next bell is Friday.
next_text: Next bell is Friday. Nifty expiry lands Tuesday.
caption_a:
Nifty slipped just 0.54% to 22,687.65, yet 1,969 stocks fell against 700 that rose.
FIIs sold Rs 3,458.7 Cr. DIIs bought Rs 2,891.32 Cr.
FMCG fell 1.41% and IT 1.05%.
Watch: TechM trades ex dividend on Friday.
